record.original_question: Let C1,..., Cn be(left or right) cosets of a finite group G such that U:= C1 ∪ · · · ∪ Cn is not G. Is it always true that |G \ U | ⩾ |G|/2n? Affirmative answers are known in some special cases(B. Sambale, M. Tărnăuceanu, J. Algebraic Combin., 55(2022), 979–987).

evidence.quote: Let C1,..., Cn be(left or right) cosets of a finite group G such that U:= C1 ∪ · · · ∪ Cn is not G. Is it always true that |G \ U | ⩾ |G|/2n? Affirmative answers are known in some special cases(B. Sambale, M. Tărnăuceanu, J. Algebraic Combin., 55(2022), 979–987).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $C_1, C_2, \dots, C_n$ be cosets in $G$ (each $C_i$ is either a left coset $g_iH_i$ or a right coset $H_ig_i$ of some subgroup $H_i \le G$, allowed to differ from one $i$ to another). Assume that the union $U := C_1 \cup C_2 \cup \cdots \cup C_n$ is a proper subset of $G$, i.e., $U \ne G$. Determine whether the inequality
$$|G \setminus U| \;\ge\; \frac{|G|}{2^n}$$
holds for every such finite group $G$ and every such choice of cosets $C_1, \dots, C_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a conjecture of Sambale and Tărnăuceanu (J. Algebraic Combin. 55 (2022), 979–987), who proved it in special cases (e.g., elementary abelian groups, where the bound (2^n-1)/2^n is shown to be sharp) and established a weaker general bound |G|/(2·n!). No general resolution appears to be available in the literature as of 2026; the problem remains posed as an open question in current group-theory problem collections.

status_evidence.title: On the size of coset unions
status_evidence.snippet: Sambale and Tărnăuceanu prove |G\U| ≥ |G|/(2·n!) in general and conjecture the sharper bound |G|/2^n, verifying it in special cases such as elementary abelian groups.
status_evidence.claim: The bound |G|/2^n is conjectured and proved only in special cases.

status_evidence.title: On the size of coset unions (repository copy)
status_evidence.snippet: Authors investigate the conjecture that |G|/2^n elements lie outside the union of n cosets when the union is proper, obtaining best possible bound for elementary abelian groups.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture remains open beyond special cases.
